## M4 — The fast tick, step by step

### M4.A Standing load

**M4.A.1** Every person **MUST** take, each tick, a load from **every** tie, whether or not any event occurred on it, as a function of that tie's bond energy divided by the receiver's `functional_level`. → §7.2. The load **MUST** be computed as the "too little" side of `M4.C.1`'s deviation function (`M4.C.1c`), with bond energy and `functional_level` entering through it; a separate standing-load formula is withdrawn.

**M4.A.2** A `TRIGGER` event **MUST** be able to spike the standing term with no contact at all with the cut-off person.

**M4.A.3** A `RECONCILIATION` event **MUST** convert standing load back into interaction-driven load.

**M4.A.4** `INSTITUTIONALIZE` **MUST** be implemented as converting a member's ties to worry edges — non-interactive, bond energy retained — and **MUST NOT** require new machinery beyond M4.A.1.

**M4.A.5** — *a **self-generated** stress term **MUST** exist, derived from `basic_level`.* Two sources of chronic stress are named and both scale with level; the model has only the inter-person one (M4.A.1) and nothing intra-person, so a person alone in a calm system currently has no load at all. Each person **MUST** therefore take, each tick, a second standing load that is a function of `basic_level` only. It **MUST** be derived, never independently parameterised (M10.A.1), and it **MUST NOT** be large enough to swamp M4.A.1 — otherwise `M11.C.1` passes for the wrong reason, on a term that never touches a tie. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe08.md` · FE08.5

### M4.B Perceive

**M4.B.1** A person **MUST** read events addressed to it *and* events it witnessed (M1.F.5).

**M4.B.2** — *what the policy may read.* The policy (`M4.D`) **MUST** compute a Person's outcome from only (a) that Person's own state; (b) that Person's beliefs, including its belief about any tie it is not party to (`M9.8`); and (c) events delivered to that Person's inbox as target or witness, after per-hop fidelity (`M1.F.4`). It **MUST NOT** read another Person's true state, the true state of a tie it is not party to, or an undelivered event. `M9.7` makes belief a channel into appraisal; this makes it the only route into selection. `M11.C.36` carries the mutant. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C9

**M4.B.2a** — *`M4.B.2` row by row, against the requirements that read true state.*

| Requirement | Reads | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `M5.F.1` receivers read the actor's `outside_ness` | another person's hidden state | Conforms: `outside_ness` acts **through the event** — it scales the delivered event's impingement component — and the receiver appraises the event. No receiver reads the field (`M5.F.1` amended) |
| `M5.C` "system calm" | family-wide tension | The triangle clause is superseded by amended `M1.C.3`. The projection clause is Phase D content and, when built, reads through belief |
| `M5.C` "marital distance high" | the marital tie | The spouses read it as their own tie. Anyone else reads it through belief (`M9.8`). Built as an engine-side gate on the effect of moves, not a policy read, so it reads the tie itself |
| `M5.C` "decision ownership held externally" | external agent state | Phase D (`M7.D.4`) |
| `M8.1` `positions_live` | `fused_into` across the group | An engine-side predicate, not a policy read. The policy **MUST NOT** call it; `M11.D.17` checks this statically |
| `M4.D.2` the person's position in the active triangle | tension on ties the person is not party to | Through belief (`M9.8`), which revision 12 places in Phase C |

**M4.B.3** — *the policy does not know consequences.* The policy (`M4.D`) **MUST NOT** contain any representation of a move's consequences beyond `M4.D.6b`'s horizon: no look-ahead, no model of the family, and no term that values a move by its effect on anyone's state beyond that horizon. A deferred cost **MUST** reach the policy only as felt anxiety when it arrives, credited to whatever moves fall inside the horizon at that time. Agents do not know that distance relieves now and costs later, or that projection calms a parent and later troubles the child; they feel their own state change and repeat what relieved it. `M11.D.22`'s static check **SHOULD** be extended to fail if the policy module reads any quantity indexed by future time. The self-directed channel is outside this rule: its objective is `M5.F.5`'s position, not a forecast. → `model_explainer.md` §19

### M4.C Appraise

**M4.C.1** — *anxiety on a tie rises with deviation from the person's felt contact optimum, in either direction.* Each person **MUST** hold, for each of its ties, a felt contact optimum, and acute anxiety **MUST** rise with the tie's deviation from it on **either** side: too little contact (rejection, isolation, the tie's absence) and too much impingement (intrusion, control, being smothered). These two drives are given, are the same for every person, and **MUST NOT** be learned. An incoming event **MUST** be appraised by the change it makes to the receiver's deviation, scaled by the tie's `conductance`, modulated by `route` (M1.F.3) and `source_position` (M1.F.2), and attenuated by `fidelity` (M1.F.4). Each move type **MUST** declare in config its effect on each side — a contact component and an impingement component, `[I]` — and **MUST** be able to carry both at once: conflict is a pattern in which "people **maintain contact and enforce distance at the same time**" (`kerr_book/ks04.md` · KS04.13). Source: "human beings have a **profound need for emotional closeness but are adverse to too much of it**… Threats of too much distance **and** too much closeness activate the stress response" (`ks03.md` · KS03.2), and threats to adequate contact and to sufficient distance "appear to be the **fundamental triggers of anxiety**" (`ks06.md` · KS06.3) — `[T]`, Kerr 2019, attribution `[K]`. → `model_explainer.md` §19

**M4.C.1a** — *level sets the steepness and the width.* The steepness with which anxiety rises with deviation **MUST** fall as `functional_level` rises, and the width of the band tolerated without anxiety **MUST** grow with it — "**well-differentiated people manage the closeness-distance dilemma more effectively**… poorly differentiated people are very prone to shut down and distance or to react aggressively" (`ks03.md` · KS03.2, `[D]`). Division by `functional_level` is one admissible steepness. Both **MUST** be derived from `functional_level` (`M10.A`), never parameterised per person; the functional forms are `[I]`. When the social cues are on, level also sets the two terms of `M4.C.14`, sensitivity and meaning error, by the same rule: derived from `functional_level`, never parameterised per person (`M10.A.1`).

**M4.C.1b** — *anxiety moves the optimum toward closeness.* As acute anxiety rises, a person's contact optimum on its loaded ties **MUST** move toward more contact: "**automatic intensification of the togetherness force is the default mode**" (`ks06.md` · KS06.5, `[T]` `[D]`). The rate is `[I]`.

**M4.C.1c** — *the standing load is the "too little" side of the same function.* `M4.A.1`'s standing load **MUST** be computed as the "too little" side of `M4.C.1`'s deviation function, evaluated every tick on every tie whether or not an event occurred, with the tie's `bond_energy` setting how much the tie matters: a cut-off tie with high bond energy stands far below its optimum. The "too little" deviation of a severed or distanced tie **MUST** build over time since contact, at an `[I]` rate, and **MUST** be spiked by a `TRIGGER` or nodal event (`M4.A.2`), rather than arriving in full at the act. Removing the impingement side is immediate. So `CUTOFF` relieves at once and costs later, which is `M11.C.4`'s shape, and the cost is real without a rule written for it. The nodal-event spike (the owner, 2026-10-17: "cut ties, as TRIGGER"): when a nodal event reaches a person (`M1.A.4k`'s reading of reach), each of their cut-off ties (in state `CUT_OFF`, `M1.B.3c`, `M1.D.2b`) between two living people takes a spike of `nodal_spike_intensity` (1.0, `[I]`, the Phase B script's `TRIGGER` size) on its standing term for the event's week, the next tick, felt by both members as a `TRIGGER`'s is (`event_effects.nodal_spike`). Spikes from separate events in one week add up, as `TRIGGER`s do. *Narrowed at the review of 2026-10-17 (Claude's recommendation, kept by the owner 2026-10-19):* the form the owner approved also counted a tie that is only not interactive as cut, which would spike a retired coach's tie, a removed member's while away, and criterion arms' switched-off ties; none of those is a cutoff in the model. The reconnection pull: while a tie is cut (`M1.B.3c`), its "too little" side **MUST** keep growing for both members, since contact is refused, and an accepted approach **MUST** relieve it. This is what draws a cut tie back toward contact; no separate pull term is written. One function **MUST** serve both; a second, separate standing-load formula is a failing implementation. This is what makes `CUTOFF` and `DISTANCE` create anxiety of their own, from lack of the relationship, with no rule written for it. A person holding a principled cutoff (`M1.B.3d`) **MUST NOT** feel this term on that tie.

**M4.C.1d** — *contact that relieves its receiver returns in part to its sender.* When a move whose contact component is positive (`M4.C.1`; `config/bowen/event_kinds.md`) is delivered to its target and relieves the target — the target's two-sided deviation on the tie (`M4.C.1`) is lower after the delivery than before, contact and impingement together — a share `reciprocal_contact_share` of the contact the target took in (`M4.C.1`'s Δ contact: the move's contact component after the tie's conductance, route and fidelity, the target's `M4.C.2` gain and `M5.F.1`'s discount) **MUST** be added to the sender's felt contact on the same tie in the same step, and the sender **MUST** appraise it as any delivered contact is appraised: by the change in their own deviation, at their own steepness (`M4.C.1a`), through `appraisal_gain`, reattribution (`M4.C.6`), attention and their own `M4.C.2` gain, with no second scaling by conductance, which the target's share already carries. Each party's `M4.C.2` gain applies to what that party takes in, so it is applied once at each end. A target whose deviation does not fall returns nothing. Relief is judged for each delivery against the target's state before the tick's batch (`M1.F.8`), as every appraisal is, and the returns from several deliveries in one tick add. The rule names no kind: it applies to every such move, sender and target, an external agent included (`SPLIT`, `FRAME_AMBIGUITY`, `DISPLACE`); the returned contact is felt contact, not `investment` (`M1.B.8`), so `M1.E.7e`'s thin coach tie is unaffected. A sender whom anxiety has moved toward closeness (`M4.C.1b`) and who stands on the "too little" side feels the returned contact as relief; one near their optimum feels little, and one within its band or past it nothing: the band is not felt, and the "too much" side of `M4.C.1`'s deviation is impingement, which the returned contact does not carry. The learner (`M4.D.6`) already credits the sender's own change in acute anxiety, so the returned contact reaches the value of the act that drew it without a change to the learner. The insiders of a triangle are calmed by their alliance (`KS03.1`, `[K]` `[T]`), and closeness is wanted as well as aversive (`KS03.2`, `[K]` `[T]`); that the calm reaches the one who sought the contact is the direction those passages give (`[K]` `[D]`). The relief condition, the share, the timing and reading it through the sender's own gain are `[I]`; the share's value is in `config/bowen/constants.md` (`M10.C.1a`). Nothing sets a `TRIANGLE`'s relief or compares it with `DISTANCE`'s. → `M4.C.1`, `M4.C.1b`, `M4.C.2`, `M4.D.6`, `M1.C.1`, `M11.C.42`, `M11.C.45`

**M4.C.1e** — *an event is read as a cue vector; the cues move the two drives and are not drives.* When the social cues are on (`M4.C.1f`), a move delivered to its target **MUST** also be read as a **perceived cue vector** over four cues — attention, approval, expectations, distress — each in [−1, 1], the threat pole negative: lack of attention, disapproval, an expectation placed on the receiver, upset in the sender. The perceived vector is the receiver's weighted reading of the four signal channels (`M4.C.11`), after detection and the meaning error (`M4.C.12`, `M4.C.14`). Each cue **MUST** move the receiver's felt contact and felt impingement through two weights held in config, scaled as the move's own components are (`conductance`, `route`, `fidelity`, intensity), and added to the move kind's two components (`M4.C.1`): a cue at its threat pole lowers felt contact by its contact weight and raises felt impingement by its impingement weight; at its other pole it does the reverse. The weights' signs are directions from the sources and their sizes are `[I]`:

**M4.C.1f** — *the reduction, and the switch.* The social cues (`M1.F.1c`, `M4.C.1e`, `M4.C.11`–`M4.C.15`, `M9.9`) **MUST** be behind one config switch, `social_cues_enabled`, which is **off** by default. With it off, a run **MUST** produce the same log as the engine before this revision, record for record (the golden fingerprints, `tests/bowen/test_engine_golden.py`, unchanged), and **MUST** make no draw of the `cue_perception` class (`M3.D.4a`). With it on, with the three nonverbal channels empty, no meaning error and full detection, each move's felt change **MUST** equal the change with it off, for every move kind. This holds by construction under the deviation form (plan D1): the word channel carries no cue, so with nothing on the other channels the cue reading adds nothing. Turning the switch on by default is an owner decision, and it moves every record. `[I]`, an engineering rule. The `M11.C` criteria that test the cues (`M11.C.50`–`M11.C.55`) run both their arms with the switch on.

| Cue | Felt contact | Felt impingement | Basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| attention | yes | no | `KS10.1`: inadequate attention triggers "rejection, panic, and emotional isolation"; `FE03.3`'s too-little set; `[K]` `[D]` |
| approval | yes, smaller | yes, larger | `M4.C.5`'s reading of criticism; `FE03.3`'s too-little set includes feeling unloved and rejected; `[K]` `[D]`; the split `[I]` (Q2) |
| expectations | no | yes | `KS08.4`: the expectation in the voice; `M1.A.9a`'s outward axis; `[K]` `[D]` |
| distress | no | yes | `KS10.1`'s "upset or equanimity in the other"; the side `[X]`: the corpus does not say which side another's distress acts on (Q3) |

The four cues are readings of a received signal. They **MUST NOT** become drives, set points or goals: `M4.C.1`'s two drives remain the only drives, and the cue reading **MUST NOT** write any person field the policy reads other than through felt contact, felt impingement and acute anxiety (`M9.9`'s belief is the one store the reading writes). The list is open — "and certainly other cues as well" (`KS10.1`) — and a cue added later is a reading, not a drive. Sources for the list: `KS01.7`, `KS07.6`, `KS09.4`, `KS10.1`, `KS23.1` (`[T]` `[K]`): people are sensitive to "approval, attention, expectations, and distress", and "the less 'self' people have, the more they are governed by reactions to such real or imagined cues" (`kerr_book/ks01.md` · KS01.7). Kerr calls them "the most common threats people experience" (`KS10.1`), not fundamental; the fundamental triggers stay `M4.C.1`'s two (`KS03.2`, `KS06.3`). A held expectation that goes unmet reads on the too-little side: a received attention or approval cue below the receiver's belief about that partner (`M9.9`) lowers felt contact by the shortfall times an `[I]` weight (`KS10.1`'s "expectations met or unmet"; `KS08.4`, the mother's anxiety at the daughter's silence; `[K]` `[D]`).

**M4.C.2** Appraisal **MUST** apply a gain function on anxiety: above threshold, event content **MUST** be defended against rather than absorbed. A plain product is a failing implementation. → §3.4

**M4.C.3** Symptom onset **MUST** be driven by an **integrator over chronicity**, not by a test on instantaneous anxiety. → §3.3

**M4.C.3a** — *the integrand is **time above the floor**, not peak.* The integrator **MUST** accumulate the excess of `acute_anxiety` above the person's usual excess (the floor is the usual level, `M1.A.5e`), where positive, so that **many resolved excursions and one unresolved excursion are distinguishable**. Citing McEwen's allostatic load: the cost is "**the wear and tear inflicted on the body due to repeated cycles of allostasis, such as occurs from repeated stresses or when the stress response system does not turn off when it should**" — **the damage is in the failure to return to baseline.** → `kerr_book/ks23.md` · KS23.3 A family's steady state is not a symptom in itself. A rise that lasts becomes usual within about a year, so a symptom nothing holds remits; what can hold one is lock-in (`M7.D.2a`).
Duration is independently supported: enduring problems "**one month or longer**" were the most frequent threats, and "**the longer the stressful life event or events lasted, the greater the risk**" (`ks23.md` · KS23.5).

**M4.C.8** — *attending to a channel **amplifies** it.* Directing attention at the feeling channel **MUST** increase its activity, not discharge it; directing it at the intellectual channel **MUST** order it. This is where feelings legitimately enter the model — **not as state** (forbidden by M1.A.0) but as a **target of attention with an amplifying effect**. → `kb/kb12.md` · K12.6

**M4.C.8a** — *the amplification **MUST** be gated by objectivity.* As M4.C.8 stands, **every** act of reflection is an escalation, which would make `M1.E.7c`'s category supply and its delayed self-observation impossible — the person could never look at their own process without inflaming it. The gate is the **stance** of the attention, not its target: attention paid **from inside** the reaction amplifies; attention paid with the observing distance M1.A.9 measures does not. `outside_ness` **MUST** therefore scale M4.C.8's amplification toward zero, and a scalar implementation that amplifies unconditionally is a failing implementation. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe03.md` · FE03.6
**This generalises `C1` beyond symptom relief**: attending to a channel is itself an intervention on it, so a coach or family member who focuses on the feeling channel **MUST** raise it. It is also the mechanism behind `M4.C.2`'s gain function seen from the other side.

**M4.C.4** `systems_perspective` (M1.A.18) **MUST** fall with acute anxiety. Polarity capture is a **loss** in someone who had the perspective, not merely a correlate of never having had it: the KB07 interview holds that systems thinking has no place for polarized debate, and that anyone locked into a polarity has either not yet reached systems thinking or reached it and lost it; and the KB12 interview, that the better a person functions, the further they can see past polarities, and the worse, the more they are caught in them. → `kb/kb07.md` · K07.6, `kb/kb12.md` · K12.7

**M4.C.6** — *reappraisal **MUST** be self-attribution, not re-interpretation of the other.* An agent with `systems_perspective` **MUST** attribute part of a received event to **its own prior emission on that tie**. The shift is not "she is not hostile" but *part of what I am receiving is my own output returning*. This is why the effect is **immediate** — no new information arrives, only a re-attribution of existing information. → `kerr_book/ks17.md` · KS17.3

When the social cues are on, the part of a received move that an agent with `systems_perspective` attributes to its own prior emission **MUST** be the **nonverbal** part — the felt change that tone, face and posture carry — in proportion to the agent's own recent nonverbal leak on that tie, against the other's, over `reappraisal_window`; the words part (the move kind's components) is not reattributed. What he took to be a tense expression on his wife's face "reflected his own facial expression and tone of voice, which in turn were intensified by what he saw in her" (`kerr_book/ks17.md` · KS17.3, `[K]` `[T]` `[M]`). The share's form is `[I]`. With the cues off, the rule is as it stands. Criterion: `M11.C.52`.

**M4.C.7** — *`route` (M1.F.3) **MUST** modulate appraisal on **both** sides.* A statement **addressed to a third party and witnessed** by the other **MUST** produce lower reactivity in the **listener** *and* in the **speaker** than the same content addressed directly. `M1.F.5` already distinguishes addressed from witnessed; this makes the witnessed form systematically less reactive and adds the **emitting-side** effect, which the spec did not carry. → `kerr_book/ks18.md` · KS18.2
This is the corpus's cleanest demonstration because **the content is identical by construction** — only the addressing changes.

**M4.C.5** The **inward-impingement** axis of M1.A.9a **MUST** have a **perception-side** readout computed at appraisal, before any move is emitted: reading the other's event as critical is itself the evidence. The KB05 interview describes people taking years to reach the point of being with their mother without taking what she says as criticism, and reads hearing a parent as critical as a sign that the hearer is probably being critical or defensive. → `kb/kb05.md` · K05.8. This readout is cheaper and harder to game than one taken from the emitted move. When the social cues are on, the impingement a delivered move adds includes its cue reading (`M4.C.1e`), so reading a neutral event as disapproving (`M4.C.12`) is read here as criticism heard: the perception side of the inward axis.

**M4.C.9** — *a witness appraises from its own position.* A witness's appraisal of an Event (`M1.F.5`) **MUST** be computed from the witness's own state, the witness's ties to **both** the sender and each target, and the intensity of the exchange between them, with a witness-specific weighting constant graded `[I]`. It **MUST NOT** be a fidelity-scaled copy of a target's appraisal. `M4.C.1` names one conductance and does not say which tie's applies to a witness; this supplies it. `M4.C.7` (the witnessed form is less reactive) and per-hop fidelity (`M1.F.4`) still apply. The source model's pull toward its bounds as absorbing states is a property of its functional form and **MUST NOT** be imported with the rule. `M11.C.35` is the test. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C8 When the social cues are on, a witness reads all four signal channels from its own position, through `M4.C.11`, `M4.C.12` and `M4.C.14` (Q9; `[I]` in form).

**M4.C.10** — *contact with a calmer person lowers anxiety.* A delivered event from a sender whose acute anxiety is below the receiver's **MUST** lower the receiver's acute anxiety, scaled by the tie's `conductance` and by the gap between them; form and magnitude are `[I]`. This generalises `M1.E.5`'s burden-transfer term from the external agent to every tie, and it is the ordinary mechanism by which self is lent (`M1.A.5d`). Seeking such contact is **not** a move and **MUST NOT** be written as one: approaching a calmer person relieves anxiety, so `M4.D.6` reinforces it. The term **social buffering** comes from outside the six corpus sources, and **MUST NOT** be cited as a source for this requirement until one is recorded in `theory/_EXTERNAL_MEASURES.md` or the ledger. The term **MUST** be included in `M6.I.6`'s stock-and-flow restatement (`M4.G.2a`). `M11.C.43` is the test. → `model_explainer.md` §19

**M4.C.11** — *anxiety raises the weight on the nonverbal channels.* When the social cues are on, the weight a receiver gives tone, face and posture against the words **MUST** rise with the receiver's acute anxiety above its chronic level, from a base weight to a cap below one. Direction and size `[I]`: no extraction entry says that anxiety moves weight from words to the nonverbal channels; the nearest is `KS01.7`'s "the less 'self' … the more they are governed by reactions to such real or imagined cues" (`[K]`), which is about level, not acute anxiety. Kept by the owner, `[I]`, as a premise (Q4, 2026-11-07).

**M4.C.12** — *real or imagined: the error is on meaning, never on presence.* When the social cues are on, the cue a receiver perceives on a detected signal channel **MUST** be the cue sent plus an error toward each cue's threat pole, with a spread drawn per delivery from the `cue_perception` draw class (`M3.D.4a`). The bias **MUST** grow with the receiver's acute anxiety above its chronic level, with the receiver's belief that the sender sends that cue's threat pole (`M9.9`, `M9.7`), and as `functional_level` falls (`M4.C.14`). The error changes what a signal that is there is read to mean — a neutral face read as disapproval, a tired voice read as an expectation; it **MUST NOT** create a signal on a channel where none was detected (the owner, 2026-11-07: "meaning only"). The source is "the perception (or misperception)" (`FE03.3`) and "real or imagined" cues (`KS01.7`, `KS07.6`), `[K]` `[T]`; the form is `[I]`. `M4.C.1c`'s too-little side already carries the reading of an absence, and is unchanged. Criterion: `M11.C.51`.

**M4.C.13** — *words are chosen; tone, face and posture leak.* When the social cues are on, the sender's tone, face and posture **MUST** carry a leak toward the threat poles of expectations and distress that grows with the sender's acute anxiety above its chronic level, saturating at `defence_threshold` (`M4.C.2`); the sender does not choose it, and no policy reads or sets it. A more differentiated sender leaks less only because its acute anxiety is lower; no separate level term is added (`M10.A.1`). The leak is the channel along which `M4.C.10`'s calmer-sender effect travels. Source: the mother's phone message, where "the anxiety in her voice and her message amounted to an expectation that the daughter call her", and the changed message, near-identical in words with a lighthearted delivery, "erased a decades-old emotional cue" (`kerr_book/ks08.md` · KS08.4, `[K]` `[T]` `[M]`). The leak's size, its split between the two cues and the three channels' shares are `[I]`. Criterion: `M11.C.50`.

**M4.C.14** — *differentiation changes sensitivity and meaning error by degree, and removes neither.* When the social cues are on, two terms **MUST** be derived from the receiver's `functional_level` (`M10.A.1`), beside `M4.C.1a`'s steepness:

**M4.C.15** — *attention is finite.* When the social cues are on, the attention cue on a sender's tone, face and posture **MUST** fall toward its threat pole with the load of the lasting exogenous stressors on the sender this week (`M1.F.6`), so that an outside preoccupation is read by the people around it as less attention. Source: a partner's preoccupation with work leaves the other "feeling inadequately attended to", and an outside stressor becomes an inside one (`kerr_book/ks07.md` · KS07.6, `[K]` `[T]`). **This is a proxy.** `M1.A.10`'s `life_energy`, zero-sum between relationship-seeking and goal-directed activity, is not built (`M6.I.3`); when it is built, this rule's bound **MUST** become the relationship share of `life_energy`, and the proxy is retired. Form and size `[I]`. Criterion: `M11.C.53`.

- **sensitivity** — how readily a nonverbal signal is detected — **MUST** rise as level falls. It is accurate about one thing: that a signal is being sent. It **MUST NOT** add meaning.
- **meaning error** — the spread and the threat bias of `M4.C.12` — **MUST** rise as level falls.

Neither term, nor the steepness, **MUST** reach zero at any level: the sensitivities "are part of all people" (`KS01.7`). Sources: people with more self have "less intense reactions, more accurate perceptions" (`KS09.4`, `[K]` `[T]`); the impaired child "read" the mother's signals and the mother read hers equally well (`ch18.md` line 42, `[B]` `[T]`). The two hold together once sensitivity and meaning accuracy are two terms (the owner, 2026-11-07, Q5: lower differentiation means more sensitivity to a signal, which is accurate that a signal is being sent, not about what it means): `[D]` for the two directions, from the two sources together; every form and size `[I]`.

### M4.D Select

**M4.D.1** Each person **MUST** resolve exactly one **outcome** per fast tick, by softmax over propensity scores. An outcome is either an emitted move (M5.A.1) or a **withheld** move (M4.D.1b).

**M4.D.1b** — *`WITHHOLD` **MUST** exist as an outcome distinct from every move in M5.A.1 and from M4.D.5's fused default.* The automatic channel's move **MUST** be computed, detected, and **not emitted**; and **a withheld move MUST still change tie state.** An implementation in which not acting is a no-op cannot represent the two canonical instances in the corpus. → `kerr_book/ks08.md` · KS08.1, `ks16.md` · KS16.2

**M4.D.1c** — *`WITHHOLD` is **not** a weak `I-POSITION`, and on its own it is **insufficient**.* Kerr's three-year trajectory runs **counter-argument** ("accomplished nothing") → **non-reaction** ("**an insufficient response to her**") → **position** (lands, reaction, resolution). `M11.C` **MUST** assert that a `WITHHOLD`-only arm does not produce the `M5.E` resolution an `I-POSITION` arm produces. → `ks16.md` · KS16.1

**M4.D.1d** — *unresolved competition between candidate moves **MUST** itself raise `acute_anxiety`*, independently of which outcome resolves. Both parties in a loaded tie hold **simultaneous** approach and withdraw urges — responsibility for the other's distress pulling toward, fear of entanglement pulling away — and "**The conflicting urges raise each person's anxiety, which further infects their interactions.**" Implementable as an entropy or margin term over the propensity distribution fed back into M1.A.8; it produces the observed vicious circle without a separate rule. → `ks06.md` · KS06.4

**M4.D.1e** — *the legal set is formed before selection.* For each person each fast tick, the policy **MUST** compute the set of legal outcomes from current tie and triangle state — the structural preconditions of each move (for example, `CUTOFF` requires a live tie, `TRIANGLE` a reachable third party, `PURSUE` a target not cut off) and every `M5.C` gate that removes a move from the draw — and **MUST** select only over that set, with weights renormalised over it. A gate that degrades a move rather than removing it (`M5.C.1`'s `outside_ness` row) is not part of the mask. The mask is logged (`M16.A.3b`). → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C11

**M4.D.1f** — *tie-break and fallback are declared, keyed and flagged.* The policy **MUST** declare a tie-break rule for equal scores and a fallback rule for a non-finite score, exhausted `life_energy` and an empty legal set. Both rules are `[I]` and **MUST** be declared in config; any draw either makes **MUST** use a key declared in `M3.D.4b`. Every selection record **MUST** state whether its outcome came from the scored policy, the tie-break or the fallback (`M16.A.3c`), because a fallback rule can generate the very behaviour a criterion tests. `M11.D.18` is the guard. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C12

**M4.D.1g** — *focus steers whom anxious acts land on.* In the automatic channel (`M4.D.1a`), each outcome of a kind that moves toward a person **MUST** have its weight multiplied by 1 + `focus_steer_gain` × the actor's investment share on the tie to that person (`M1.B.8`, `[I]`), rescaled so the kind's total weight over its automatic outcomes is unchanged. Focus changes whom an act lands on, not how often the kind is chosen; unscaled, it also raised the projection kinds' total weight, which `M11.C.2` and `M11.C.6` count (learning-qa review 2026-10-14). Those kinds are the `projection` row of `config/bowen/pattern_acts.md`: `OVERFUNCTION`, `PURSUE`, `TRIANGLE`. Withdrawing kinds, `CUTOFF` and `DISTANCE` among them, are not steered. Investment is valence-blind, so a cut tie holds investment, and steering every kind would send more cutoffs toward ties already cut. The self channel **MUST NOT** be steered. Competing urges (`M4.D.1d`) read the unsteered weights, as now. Without this, focus moves anxiety but not acts: measured 2026-10-13 (ad hoc, plan §4.7), the reference family's parents spread projection-type acts evenly over three children. It applies in every run.

**M4.D.1h** — *an anxious act lands with more force.* The owner (2026-10-14): people "can become demanding to the point of being abusive, either because of tremendous stress or low level of differentiation"; their choice, "force rises with anxiety". An automatic act's intensity **MUST** be `policy_intensity` × (1 + `force_anxiety_gain` × a ÷ (a + 100)), a the actor's excess anxiety (acute above chronic). A self-directed act keeps `policy_intensity`. The intensity carries into everything that reads it — the intrusion, a cutoff's rejection, a refusal, a functioning move — not only danger; a scripted act keeps the intensity its criterion gives it. It saturates at (1 + `force_anxiety_gain`) times: unbounded, force and the other's anxiety fed each other and a run diverged within 23 weeks. Excess rather than excess above usual: the usual level follows a chronically stressed person up, and force read from it barely moved (both measured 2026-10-14, plan §4.10). Level enters through anxiety, which rises more steeply in a less differentiated person (`M4.C.1a`). It applies in every run.

**M4.D.1a** — *selection **MUST** run over **two channels with different objectives**, not one.* The **automatic** channel is driven by the relationship system, its objective is to discharge anxiety **now**, and it carries the seven reactive moves. The **self-directed** channel is driven by the person, its objective is to hold a position **through** discomfort (M5.F.5), and it carries `I-POSITION` and `STAY-IN-CONTACT`. The **mixing weight between them MUST be a function of differentiation**: at low level the person is nearly all automatic, and as level rises a real self-directed channel opens. Agency is **not absent** — it is graded, and the higher the level the less the individual is governed by what the system wants. The mixing weight **MUST** read `systems_perspective` as well as `functional_level`: `w = f + perspective_channel_gain × perspective × (1 − f)`, with `f` as before, so a person with perspective chooses the self-directed channel more often at the same level, and one with none behaves exactly as before. Perspective **MUST** also steer within the channels: the weight of each act listed in config is scaled by `1 ± perspective_steer_gain × perspective` — away from `TRIANGLE` and `CONFLICT` ("don't triangle … not to blame", the owner), toward `DETRIANGLE` and `PREVENT_ALIGNMENT` ("know to detriangle").
**Consequence, and its evidence is the spec's own reasoning rather than the passage below.** Differentiation is **not reachable by lengthening a reinforcement horizon**, because the two channels optimise different things and the target is not in the automatic channel's objective at all. *Flagged 2026-08-28: the KB10 passage below does not assert this, and the corpus arguably cuts the other way — the actions that can make a system more flexible "are based on a **broad and long-range assessment** of the situation" (`family_evaluation/fe03.md` · FE03.21, Kerr's chapter, `[K]`). The passage supports "relieving now worsens later"; it does not establish that a longer horizon cannot reach the target. The claim stands as a design decision, `[I]`, not as a corpus finding. The passage itself is also **societal** in scope — the KB10 interview on band-aid legislation — and individual-level support exists elsewhere in the corpus and should replace it.* This is what M4.D.6d and M11.C.17 assert. Anxiety-relieving action genuinely relieves anxiety — the KB10 interview describes band-aid laws passed to ease immediate anxiety and says that the more of them are passed, the more they feed the very problem they were meant to fix — so an agent selecting a binder is not making an error a longer horizon would correct. → `kb/kb10.md` · K10.7; M1.A.0 (the moves are instinct-level, not feeling-states)
The automatic channel learns from felt relief over a short horizon (`M4.D.6a`), so the horizon argument above does not carry weight. The two-channel design stands for its own reason: the self-directed channel's objective is `M5.F.5`'s position, which is not in the automatic channel's objective at any horizon, and `M4.D.6d` keeps that channel out of reinforcement.
The self-directed channel also carries the four family moves of `M5.B` — `DETRIANGLE`, `PREVENT_ALIGNMENT`, `REDUCE_CUTOFF` and `PROVOKE` — scored by the same position gap as `I-POSITION` (`M5.F.5`).

**M4.D.2** The propensity score **MUST** be a function of acute anxiety, `functional_level`, the state of the tie in question, the person's position in the active triangle, and their learned repertoire.

**M4.D.3** Rising anxiety **MUST** raise the weight on the seven reactive moves. **Through two routes, neither of them a written weight.** (a) Anxiety lowers `functional_level`, which shifts `M4.D.1a`'s mixing weight toward the automatic channel. (b) Within the automatic channel, a move's learned value (`M4.D.6`) **MAY** be conditioned on the person's acute anxiety, so that acts which relieved under high anxiety are chosen under high anxiety. The policy **MUST NOT** carry a separate term that raises reactive weights with anxiety.

**M4.D.3a** — *the repertoire **MUST** carry a **complexity ordering**, and rising anxiety **MUST** slide selection down it.* A binary reactive/non-reactive split is too coarse. The ordering, from the source: **cooperation** ("a complex behavior… that requires the intellectual and emotional systems to function as a working team") → **conflict** → **dominant-adaptive** ("older evolutionarily, more primitive") → **distance**, the oldest ("single-celled organisms could not survive without a distancing mechanism"). Regression is "**dominated by less thoughtful and more reactive ways of interacting that are older in an evolutionary sense**". → `kerr_book/ks06.md` · KS06.1, `ks02.md` · KS02.3. The slide **MUST** come through capacity, not through an anxiety weight, so that it is consistent with amended `M4.D.3`: as anxiety lowers `functional_level`, the newer, more complex acts **MUST** lose capacity — they become less available or less effective — exposing the older layer intact (`ks23.md` · KS23.2). The ordering is a capacity limit and a gate; the policy carries no term that reads anxiety and raises the weight of older acts. `TRIANGLE` **MUST** sit in the oldest layer, with `DISTANCE` and `CUTOFF` (`config/bowen/event_kinds.md`), so falling functional level does not make a triangle less available: triangles may have roots older than language (`KS15.10`, `[K]` `[T]`), and three people together invariably gravitate to two insiders and an outsider, the well differentiated included (`FE06.20`, `[K]` `[T]`). The source orders four classes and does not place triangling among them (`KS06.1`, `KS02.3`), so the placement is `[I]` (the owner's D22, 2026-10-24); it removes a gate rather than adding a preference.
**Consequence:** the propensity vector acquires a principled shape rather than nine free weights — a derivation in M10.A.2's preferred sense — and regression becomes **loss of the newer regulatory layer exposing an intact older one**, not damage, which is why it is reversible (`ks23.md` · KS23.2).

**M4.D.3b** — *engagement with a loaded tie **MUST** be gated by `systems_perspective` (M1.A.18), not by anxiety alone.* Without mindware the loaded tie is **correctly** avoided; with it, the same tie becomes approachable. This is the fourth of the six named ingredients of the differentiating process and nothing else in the spec supplies it — M4.D.3 alone drives every move toward *less* engagement *(as written before revision 11; amended `M4.D.3` works through the mixing weight and learning)*. → `ks15.md` · KS15.1, KS15.11

**M4.D.4** Propensity for `I-POSITION` **MUST NOT** be monotonically increasing in `basic_level`. An implementation in which the highest-`basic_level` member reliably moves first is a failing implementation. → §5.2

**M4.D.5** The default state **MUST** be the fused default — each altering self to manage the other's functioning while demanding the other change — and **MUST NOT** be modelled as an absence of a move. → §5.2

**M4.D.5a** — *a per-tie **accommodation stock** **MUST** grow monotonically under the fused default and **MUST NOT** decay.* Each concession is individually small and defensible; none is reversed; the cumulative effect is the family's behaviour progressively constrained by one member's reactivity. → `kerr_book/ks19.md` · KS19.3

**M4.D.5b** — *the accommodation stock **MUST** shift the family's own reporting baseline.* "**the family learned to normalize Ted's aberrant behaviors, to weave them into the family fabric. This is part of what keeps highly influential emotional processes hidden.**" Two mothers in two unrelated families gave the same account of the years before catastrophe — "**there was nothing gross**" — and both were **sincere**. → `ks19.md` · KS19.3, KS19.8; `ks25.md` · KS25.7
**Consequence:** `M1.E`'s entry threshold is **family-relative**, not absolute, so a family whose baseline has drifted may never trigger it. That is a real dynamic for `M11.C.17`'s coach-free arm, not an artefact.

**M4.D.5c** The decision rule behind M4.D.5a **MUST** be short-horizon by construction: **Andrew Solomon**, quoted approvingly by Kerr — *not Kerr's own words, and not Bowen's*: "**All parenting involves choosing between the day… and the years.** Nancy's error seems to have been that **she always focused on the day**… her willingness to indulge his isolation **may well have exacerbated the problems it was intended to ameliorate**." This is M4.D.6a's forbidden proxy in its human form, and `M11.C.16` is the test. → `ks21.md` · KS21.1. `M4.D.6a` does not forbid this signal; the automatic channel learns on it, and this rule is the same claim in one parent. `M11.C.16` now measures repertoire concentration by level.

**M4.D.5d** — *`emotional_reserve` **MUST** be derived, and **MUST** gate symptom onset.* M4.D.5a's accommodation stock grows monotonically and currently has **no consequence** — nothing reads it. The source names the missing quantity repeatedly across two chapters: reserve is **capacity minus what is already committed to accommodation**. Therefore `emotional_reserve = f(basic_level) − accommodation_stock`, derived and never independently parameterised (M10.A.1), and symptom onset in M7.D **MUST** be gated on it rather than on absolute anxiety alone. This is what lets two agents at the same anxiety differ in whether they break, and it gives M4.D.5a the consequence it lacks. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe03.md` · FE03.10

**M4.D.6** Moves that worked before **MUST** be reinforced, so that a family develops a characteristic style. The soothing review: now and then a person **MUST** be able to ask whether soothing helped — every `soothing_review_every` weeks, with a probability rising with `basic_level` and perspective — and, where their load weeks after soothing was no lower than when they soothed, the learned value of their avoiding and soothing acts **MUST** fall. The owner: "Some people learn, eventually, that soothing isn't really the answer … from time to time … an agent should ask — is soothing helping me?" Immediate relief, which soothing always gives, is otherwise all the automatic channel learns from.

**M4.D.6a** — *the automatic channel's reinforcement signal **MUST** be the actor's felt change in acute anxiety over a short declared horizon.* The signal is that change, together with `M4.D.6e`'s cross-person term, measured over `M4.D.6b`'s horizon. It is short by design: the automatic channel's objective is to discharge anxiety now (`M4.D.1a`). Relief that keeps in place the pattern producing the anxiety is the corpus's own account — "People **blame each other for the problem, which is calming for both**… But the anxiety is now **bound** in both people" (`kerr_book/ks04.md` · KS04.13) — and `M4.D.5c`'s short-horizon decision rule is the same claim in one parent. Whether this learning drives a family's repertoire onto `CUTOFF`, or onto any single move, is a result to measure (`M11.C.16`); a rule that prevents it **MUST NOT** be added. `I-POSITION` and `STAY-IN-CONTACT` are in the self-directed channel, which `M4.D.6d` keeps out of reinforcement, so the signal does not punish them. → `model_explainer.md` §19

**M4.D.6b** The signal's horizon **MUST** be declared in config, `[I]`, and **MUST** be swept (`M17.E.1`) together with the learning rate and `M4.D.1`'s selection temperature, because a repertoire that collapses may be an artefact of the learner rather than a family process.
**The horizon belongs to `functional_level`, which is the *shorter* timescale** (M1.A.5a) — **not** to the `M1.A.4a` estimator's window. Reinforcement operates on the swing term, short relative to it — the horizon **MUST** cover the weeks over which an act's felt effect arrives, not the months over which a deferred cost arrives, because the automatic channel does not know deferred costs (`M4.B.3`); the estimator operates on `basic_level`, over years. Scaling the reinforcement horizon to the estimator window is a failing implementation. → user, G3 approval 2026-08-24

**M4.D.6c** A uniformly degenerate policy shifts both arms of a two-arm criterion together (M0.4), so it is invisible to every criterion that holds the policy fixed across arms. Under `M4.D.6a` such a policy is a possible result, not a failure to guard against; `M11.C.16` reports it per seed.

**M4.D.6d** Reinforcement **MUST** operate on the **automatic channel only** (M4.D.1a) — that is what gives a family its characteristic style. `systems_perspective` (M1.A.18) and `basic_level` (M1.A.4) **MUST NOT** be reinforcement targets, and the self-directed channel **MUST NOT** be subject to M4.D.6 at all.

**M4.D.6e** — *reinforcement **MUST** be able to arrive from another person's state.* M4.D.6 reinforces on the actor's **own** signal, so nothing in the model currently drives the projection loop's step 5, internalisation. The named mechanism is cross-person: the child learns that acting as the parental image predicts **calms the mother**, and **her calming is the reinforcement**. Therefore a move's reinforcement signal **MUST** be able to include the change in a **witness's or target's** anxiety, not only the actor's, and the projection target's repertoire **MUST** shape itself to that signal. This is what makes `M11.C.2`'s concentration a learned outcome rather than an assigned one. It remains inside M4.D.6d: the channel reinforced is still the automatic one. *Decided 2026-10-09 (owner):* a `TRIANGLE`'s recruited third is **not** in its cross-person term — the seeker learns from the seeker's own relief; this term is the projection account, not a recruit's distress. → `theory/family_evaluation/fe07.md` · FE07.4 The cross-person term is the others' relief weighted by the actor's bond energy on its tie to each, so a child's tie to a parent outweighs a thin tie to a witness; a person with no tie to the actor carries no weight. No rule names a parent

**M4.D.6f** — *learning from what a witnessed cutoff does.* The owner (2026-10-13): "add learning by witnessing cutoff", then: "It depends on what the witness sees happen to the cutoff person and others", and "Principled cutoff should teach that this is good action (it's functioning up)." When a person is delivered a `CUTOFF` as a witness (`M1.F.5`), the witness **MUST** keep a record of it, with the functional level at that moment of each family member they hold a tie to: the cutter, the person cut off and the others. `witness_window` weeks later (`[I]`), the witness's automatic channel's learned value of `CUTOFF` **MUST** take a step of `witnessed_cutoff_gain` toward the change seen (`[I]`): `value ← value + witnessed_cutoff_gain × (change seen − value)`, `M4.D.6a`'s form. The change seen is the bond-energy-weighted mean change in those people's functional levels. The weight of each is the bond energy of the witness's tie to them ÷ the sum over those ties; an external agent is excluded.
- If the family functions better after the cutoff, the value rises; if it functions worse, it falls.
- The kind of cutoff is not read. A principled cutoff that lets the cutter function up teaches that cutoff is a good act, as the owner states. A reactive cutoff whose cost (`M1.B.3d`) pulls the cutter and the family down teaches against it.
- The move applies to every learned value for `CUTOFF` in the witness's current anxiety band, in every position, toward each family member they hold a tie to. Because it is a step toward the change seen, repeated witnessing cannot carry a value past what the witness has seen.

This is learning from another's consequences, not copying: the witness does not learn that cutoff happened, but what followed it. The witness can learn only `CUTOFF`. A person's own cutoff is principled when declared (`M1.B.3d`) or in proportion to the danger they feel from the person cut off (`M1.B.3e`). Otherwise learning that cutoff is good raises a `CUTOFF` propensity that is reactive when the policy selects it. That narrower gap is stated, not closed

### M4.E Act

**M4.E.1** A selected move **MUST** become an event with sender, targets, witnesses, intensity, timestamp, route, fidelity and the tie's latency.

**M1.F.1a** — *the event record **MUST** carry the **channel** that selected the move* — `AUTOMATIC` or `SELF_DIRECTED`, or a mixture weight, since "**a given decision may contain elements of both.**" → `kerr_book/ks13.md` · KS13.5
**Without it the model cannot distinguish two cases the theory says are opposite.** "Going toward a goal" and "running away from a problem" can be the **same emitted act** — a geographic move, or staying put, is uninformative in **both** directions. Only the driving channel separates them, and no readout, and not the `M1.A.4a` estimator, can recover it after the fact.
It is also what makes `M1.A.5c`'s pseudo-self sign computable.

**M4.E.1a** The `witnesses` field of the event `M4.E.1` creates **MUST** be filled by the visibility component (`M1.F.1b`), not by the policy that selected the move. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C7

### M4.G Consolidate

**M4.G.1** Repeated moves **MUST** harden tie state: three withdrawals in a row **MUST** register as a distant relationship, not as three independent events. The hardening is physics — each withdrawal lowers contact on the tie. "A distant relationship" is a pattern readout under `M5.A.1a`, not a state this rule writes. The tie state is the physics' record of the run (`consolidate`, step 9): three `DISTANCE`s in a row across a tie, uninterrupted by any other act across it, put the tie in `DISTANT`; three `CONFLICT`s in a row put it in `OPEN_CONFLICT`; either records the tie's stock as its reference level (`M1.D.2c`). A tie already `CUT_OFF`, `DISTANT` or `OPEN_CONFLICT` is left to `M1.D.2b` and `M1.D.2c`.

**M4.G.2** All invariants in M6 **MUST** be asserted at the end of every fast tick.

**M4.G.2a** — *`M6.I.6` is not asserted until it is restated.* As worded it fails on every tick: appraisal creates acute anxiety and consolidation decays it with no sink named (external review A3). `M4.G.2` therefore asserts every `M6` invariant **except** `M6.I.6`, which **MUST** remain in the invariant set as a named check that raises if enabled, so it cannot be dropped silently. Restating `M6.I.6` at the scope of bound quantities across rerouting and transfer events, with a stock-and-flow table, is a prerequisite of Phase C. `M6.I.6` is restated and `M6.4` holds the table, so from Phase C `M4.G.2` asserts every `M6` invariant, `M6.I.6` included.

**M4.G.3** — *conditional: habituation on repeated relief.* If any `M4` term credits anxiety relief to a repeated identical move within a window — reassurance-seeking `PURSUE`, checking-type `OVERFUNCTION` — that term **SHOULD** decay geometrically with the repetition count, with the decay constant graded `[I]`, or **SHOULD** be shown by sweep not to be bistable (ignored below a threshold, absorbing above it, with no graded regime between). The condition is met — `M4.D.6a` credits short-horizon relief — so this requirement binds. → `model_explainer.md` §18 · C13
